title.narrative: Tunisia Tertiary Education for Employability Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Tertiary Education for Employability Project for Tunisia is to improve the employability of tertiary education graduates and to strengthen the management of higher education. The project consists of two components. The first component, improving employability of graduates aims at improving the employability of future graduates by supporting supply side measures to better align graduates skills and competences with labor market needs. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) support a set of incentive measures, using the competitive grant scheme developed under the higher education reform project (projet d’appui à la rEforme de l’enseignement supErieu (PARES II) project competitive fund scheme for quality support program (PAQ); and (ii) a set of systemic and cross-cutting activities which will support the preparation or implementation of the PAQ grants foreseen under sub-component one. The second component, strengthening the management of higher education will combine a set of PAQ incentives and systemic measures aimed at improving the management of the higher education system. It consists of three sub-components: (i) using the PAQ competitive grant scheme developed under the PARES II project - in particular the PAQ management capacity window, to improve governance and management, quality assurance, including through support to young universities; (ii) set of systemic measures (for example with regard to strategic planning, capacity building measures for better governance, quality assurance and financial management, student admission, and a functioning higher education management and information system) to support the areas of governance and management, quality assurance, and financing; and (iii) project management unit (PMU) to reinforce its coordinating and managing capacity by recruiting - on a competitive basis - additional qualified and experienced technical staff to effectively coordinate, monitor, and evaluate activities carried out under each sub-component.
The objective of the Tertiary Education for Employability Project (TEEP) is to improve the employability of tertiary education students and to strengthen the management of higher education.

comment.narrative: This indicator focuses on the employment results published by universities and HEIs. With the generalization of the survey of 2022-2023 to all universities and all faculties, 33 HEIs have already published their results and the number is continuously progressing. The end target has been met and exceeded.

title.narrative: Public universities that have a functional internal quality assurance unit
Public universities that have a functional internal quality assurance unit

comment.narrative:
Same data maintained. The key elements of a functional internal quality assurance unit are defined as follows: (i) number of staff working in Quality Committees (CQ) within the university trained in internal quality standards according to national and international good practices and (ii) drafting of a reference manual/guide to internal quality assurance based on national standards and good practices. All universities have staff working in the QCs.
They have all been trained and certified. 9 universities have adopted their reference manual. A new detailed survey on internal quality assurance will be conducted in 1rst quarter of 2024 and will allow drawing up an updated and complete list of activities implemented by internal quality assurance units. This PDO indicator has been achieved and exceeded.

title.narrative: Proportion of students registered in higher education who choose programs that are in high demand by the Tunisian private sector

comment.narrative: Recent data from the BEPP (the Department in charge of statistics and planning of the MOHESR) shows that that 57.5% of students registered in higher education in 2024 choose programs that are in high demand by the Tunisian private sector. The list of programs in high demand by the Tunisian private sector was updated in 2024 based on the national survey on employability of graduates of higher education.
